verdict.probe_answer: Both arms' commit_precedence tests assert concrete values, not vacuous checks, and would fail against a naive precedence impl (e.g. missing Typed tier or missing comment-strip). Arm A covers Typed>File>Title>Derived + comment-only-typed→Title, but has zero coverage of the '64 KiB bound' requirement. I ran both arms' real code: Arm A's own bounding is broken — commit_message(Some("x".repeat(65537)), None, "My Title", "task") truncates to 64KiB of 'x's tagged CommitSource::Typed instead of falling back to Title (verified via cargo test). Arm B added exactly this oversize case to its suite; it passes against Arm B's reject-on-oversize impl, and fails against Arm A's — proof it's a genuine regression-catching test, not a formality, and it matches the actual merged reference implementation's semantics. Strongest test A: comment-only-typed→Title. Weakest spot in A: no test exercises bounding at all, which is exactly where its bug hides. Strongest test B: the oversize→Title case. Weakest test B: 'no typed/no file→title' — correct but trivial.
verdict.rationale: Both implement identical signatures/enum/precedence/call-site threading (main.rs, merge.rs) and correctly avoid rippling into decide()/tweak.rs per the brief. The decisive difference is the 64 KiB bound: the task says to 'mirror read_commit_msg_file's bounding', which rejects (returns None) oversized content. Arm B's commit_candidate does this (reject); Arm A's sanitize_commit_candidate instead truncates oversized input and still returns it as present. I confirmed empirically (via cargo test against each arm's actual code) that Arm A returns a 64KiB garbage commit message tagged Typed for an oversized typed candidate, where spec/reference/Arm B correctly fall back to Title. Arm B also added a test covering this exact case; Arm A did not, and lacking it let the bug ship untested.
